necessary_context.content: Finite-dimensional Euclidean E with an arbitrary norm ||·|| and dual ||·||*. Z is nonempty convex compact. F:Z→E is monotone and L-Lipschitz between these norms. Source assumes continuously differentiable omega with gradient strong monotonicity constant alpha>0. P_z(q)=argmin_{u∈Z}{omega(u)+<u,q-grad omega(z)>}.
necessary_context.name: VI geometry and exact prox

necessary_context.content: V(u,z)=omega(u)-omega(z)-<grad omega(z),u-z>; Theta(z0)=max_{u∈Z}V(u,z0). Proposition 2.2 averages evaluation points w_t with weights gamma_t. Remark 2.3 selects z0 minimizing omega and gives Theta(z0)≤max_Z omega-min_Z omega.
necessary_context.name: Bregman potential and output

necessary_context.content: Section 3 can stop its inner process after one or two prox evaluations; Theorem 3.2 establishes the safe gamma=alpha/(sqrt(2)L). The assigned fixed two-step rule is displayed as (4.2), with full-prefix average and constant safe gamma in this extraction, rather than the different Hölder tuning/half-tail average of Theorem 4.1.
necessary_context.name: Basic implementation versus fixed two-step rule
